commands.review_summary:
Adds explicit OpenClaw plugin target classification, scanner capability gating, full-directory ClawHub-profile scanning, plugin-aware judge context, documentation, and regression coverage.

Reproducibility: yes. from source and documented behavior: supply an otherwise valid OpenClaw JSON5 manifest containing a comment or trailing comma, and the branch's strict-JSON target parser fails before scanner dispatch. This review did not execute the path locally.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] Patrick-Erichsen should decide whether to sponsor the public plugin contract and require OpenClaw-compatible JSON5 parsing before merge; the remaining blocker is not solely a safe mechanical repair.

target.title: feat(runner): support OpenClaw plugins across the ClawHub profile
target.body:
## Summary

- Recognize explicit OpenClaw plugin directories or `openclaw.plugin.json` files as first-class `plugin` targets with stable manifest identity, ambiguity rejection, and symlink-hardened manifest reads.
- Give plugins parity with skills under the built-in `clawhub` profile: ClawScan Static, SkillSpector, and VirusTotal all run, and the bundled Codex judge receives production-compatible `packageRelease` evidence context.
- Preserve compatible generic scanning: Socket continues to inspect dependency manifests inside plugin directories, while unsupported skill-only scanners return an explicit `skipped` result.
- Scan the complete plugin directory: SkillSpector sees plugin code and manifest files; VirusTotal hashes/uploads a deterministic, timezone-independent `plugin.zip`; the constrained judge workspace prioritizes `openclaw.plugin.json`.

## Scope

- [x] CLI behavior
- [x] Scanner adapters
- [x] ClawHub judge/profile behavior
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Benchmark behavior
- [ ] Release/CI/repo automation

## Security / Trust Impact

Plugin contents remain untrusted throughout classification and staging. Manifest discovery uses `lstat`; manifest reads use `O_NOFOLLOW` plus a same-file re-check; identity is size-capped and validated without recording host paths. A directory containing both `SKILL.md` and `openclaw.plugin.json` fails closed as ambiguous, while an explicitly supplied manifest disambiguates the intended target.

VirusTotal parity deliberately matches existing skill behavior: a local deterministic ZIP of the full target is submitted when its hash is unknown. Standard VirusTotal uploads may enter its shared corpus, so operators should not scan confidential packages with a public key.

## Verification

- [x] `go test -count=1 ./...`
- [x] `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] Release builds: Darwin amd64/arm64, Linux amd64/arm64, Windows amd64
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Docs build/check
- [x] First-party dual-layout plugin E2E: explicit manifest classified as `plugin`; ClawScan Static scanned 15 files, omitted 0, and found 0 issues
- [x] Owned-plugin Docker E2E with the published runtime: SkillSpector scanned 3/3 files with score 0 and left no residual container
- [x] Owned-plugin full `clawhub` profile E2E: all three scanners completed with 0 failures/skips and 0 issues; VirusTotal completed its upload path; the Codex judge returned benign with high confidence
- [x] GPT-5.6-SOL xhigh branch review, with both accepted compatibility findings fixed and revalidated

## Root Cause

Target resolution only recognized skills and URLs, so plugin manifests were routed through skill assumptions. Scanner capability and artifact metadata also lacked a plugin target kind, preventing the ClawHub pipeline from safely selecting and contextualizing compatible scanners.

## Real behavior proof

After the patch, scanning an owned plugin fixture with the complete `clawhub` profile classified it as a plugin and completed ClawScan Static, SkillSpector, VirusTotal, and the Codex judge with no scanner failures or skips. An explicit manifest from a first-party dual-layout plugin also resolved as a plugin and completed the built-in static scan across all 15 eligible files with no omissions.

## What was not tested

- The stock Docker runtime does not inherit host OAuth credentials, so the complete profile's Codex judge was verified host-side; the published Docker runtime was verified separately with SkillSpector.
- VirusTotal accepted the live upload, but this run did not wait for its later shared-corpus analysis report.

## Notes

Plugins are never auto-discovered; callers must pass the plugin directory or manifest explicitly. JSON5-only manifests remain outside this change and fail with a clear strict-JSON error.
